learning_outcomes.text: After completing the module "Thermal Energy Technology", students will have detailed knowledge of the concepts of thermal energy and plant technology and their possible applications. They know the basic components of these systems and can describe, analyze, and calculate the processes, and evaluate optimization possibilities.
Students are able to distinguish individual components of an energy system and make evidence-based, qualitative and quantitative judgments on their use.

Students understand the different methods for utilizing thermal energy, they develop processes for using the appropriate method for each application and transfer solution approaches to corresponding problems.
Within the module, students transfer technical problems into a computer-aided calculation method that is also used in industry.
Students apply common calculation methods to evaluate the results and know the underlying material data, tables, and diagrams.

The technically sound analysis and evaluation of various energy conversion systems, which can be assessed and compared using different key figures, enables a sound assessment of the public discussion on the current and future energy supply situation. It also helps to derive relevant research questions for determining forecasts for assessing the effects of global energy demand and its provision.
Students present the results obtained through calculation and measurement in a written report.
Increase of social competence through comprehensive discussion of the extreme imbalances in regional and territorial energy consumption and the resulting environmental pollution.
After completing the module "Thermal Energy Technology", students know fundamental data on energy supply and are able to evaluate it with regard to future scenarios.
They can characterize different types of thermal and electrical energy provision and explain the use and potential of existing technologies.
Students are able to interpret current trends in improving the efficiency of thermal energy systems and describe the background for them.

After completing the module, students understand and apply the different boundary conditions for analyzing technical systems for the use and provision of thermal energy, energy conversion and thermal energy transport.
They can identify and evaluate suitable processes, components and procedures, and develop, discuss and justify suitable applications with regard to technical and societal challenges.

assessment_rules: The graded examination performance is a term paper of approximately 15-20 pages. The ungraded examination performance is experimental work consisting of 2-3 experiments. ECTS credits are awarded based on these performances.
